technical_explanation: All four production fail-closed checks short-circuit whenever SALES_TESTING=1 without checking SALES_ENV=='production'. jwt_secret() returns the hardcoded public string 'test-only-secret-do-not-use-for-deployment-32' before checking production mode; main.py skips assert_runtime_config() and Google Sheets initialization; sheets.py sets allow_in_memory_fallback=True (allowing direct in-memory append/update/delete); transaction_safety.py skips production TRANSACTION_DB_PATH durability and multi-instance guards.
reproducible_scenario: Set SALES_ENV=production and SALES_TESTING=1 (with SALES_JWT_SECRET unset) and start backend/app/main.py. Application starts cleanly, signs JWTs with the hardcoded public test secret, skips Google Sheets connection, enables volatile in-memory writes, and bypasses SQLite coordinator durability checks.
actual_impact: Complete collapse of production authentication confidentiality (forged tokens via public JWT secret), Single-Write-Owner enforcement, and transaction durability if SALES_TESTING=1 is accidentally set in Render.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — tests deliberately set SALES_TESTING=1 globally in backend/tests/__init__.py:10 and never test the conflict SALES_ENV=production + SALES_TESTING=1.
recommended_action: Fail hard at startup (RuntimeError) whenever SALES_ENV=='production' and SALES_TESTING=='1' are both set; never honor SALES_TESTING=1 when SALES_ENV=='production' in config.py, main.py, sheets.py, or transaction_safety.py.

technical_explanation: CANONICAL_ROLE_V2_MAP maps FACTORY_WORKER to PRODUCTION (line 82), whereas DEFAULT_ROLE_PERMISSIONS defines FACTORY_WORKER as read-only {'production': ['view']} (line 395). In has_permission() (lines 492-500), lookup iterates (v2_role, c_role, raw_role) with v2_role FIRST, so FACTORY_WORKER matches V2_ROLE_PERMISSIONS['PRODUCTION'] before DEFAULT_ROLE_PERMISSIONS['FACTORY_WORKER'].
reproducible_scenario: Authenticate a user with role='FACTORY_WORKER' in AuthUsers and call has_permission(user, 'production', 'create') or invoke production write endpoints gated by require_module_action(user, 'production', 'create'). Call succeeds with HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 403.
actual_impact: Privilege escalation: read-only factory workers receive full PRODUCTION write permissions (create batches, record consumption/output/loss/gig work, submit QC).
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — no RBAC regression test asserts FACTORY_WORKER is denied production write actions.
recommended_action: Remove FACTORY_WORKER->PRODUCTION elevation in CANONICAL_ROLE_V2_MAP or enforce explicit restricted FACTORY_WORKER permissions in V2_ROLE_PERMISSIONS and add negative RBAC tests.

technical_explanation: Unlike line 1255 (which filters tab_name != 'BillNumbers'), recover_transaction, _find_existing_sheets_allocation_for_nonce, and check_transaction_status take the first IdAllocations row matching clean_nonce via next(...) without excluding tab_name=='BillNumbers'. Even where check_transaction_status ignores BillNumbers for tab_name (line 3659), line 3664 still copies alloc_match['allocated_id'] (KS-BILL-...) into allocated_id.
reproducible_scenario: Commit a CREATE_SALE where Apps Script writes a BillNumbers row (KS-BILL-0001) before the Sales row (SALE-0001) under the same nonce in IdAllocations, then trigger timeout recovery or GET /api/v2/transactions/status/{nonce}. Lookup selects the BillNumbers row, compares KS-BILL-0001 against SALE-0001 (or searches Sales for KS-BILL-0001), and returns ALLOCATION_ID_MISMATCH or ORPHAN_ID_ALLOCATION_DETECTED.
actual_impact: False RECOVERY_REQUIRED quarantine on cleanly committed sales, locking operator forms and requiring unnecessary manual Owner reconciliation.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — test_tx_final_08 only tests standalone BillNumbers without a coexisting Sales row under the same nonce.
recommended_action: Centralize IdAllocations nonce lookup into a helper that filters out auxiliary tab_name=='BillNumbers' (or matches expected target_tab first) across all 4 call sites and add regression test with BillNumbers preceding Sales.

function_route_or_symbol: receive_raw_material; record_dal_milling_batch; create_packaging; record_workforce_payment; record_supplier_payment; create_customer_return; _verify_required_accounting_journal
technical_explanation: Unlike CREATE_SALE (sales.py:570-619), six other financial routers execute operational writes in one governed bridge call and post GL journals in a separate second bridge call without SECONDARY_QUARANTINE on failure; _verify_required_accounting_journal only enforces CREATE_SALE and RECORD_SALE_PAYMENT. Additionally, receive_raw_material replay (production.py:1018-1056) returns ALREADY_RECORDED without posting a missing journal, and record_workforce_payment (workforce.py:1683) never persists accounting_journal_ref back to WorkforcePayments.
reproducible_scenario: Simulate bridge 503/504 on post_receipt_journal, post_milling_journal, post_packaging_batch_journal, post_workforce_payment_journal, post_supplier_payment_journal, or post_customer_return_journal after the primary write commits. Operational/inventory/payment rows remain committed in Sheets while GL JournalHeaders/JournalLines are missing and coordinator state stays COMMITTED instead of RECOVERY_REQUIRED. Retrying receive_raw_material returns ALREADY_RECORDED without creating the journal.
actual_impact: Silent subledger-to-General-Ledger divergence (inventory, payables, payroll, and credit-note balances out of sync with Trial Balance) with no automatic quarantine or reconciliation queue entry.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — test_tx_final_01 tests only CREATE_SALE and RECORD_SALE_PAYMENT secondary quarantine.
recommended_action: Either move journal posting inside the single atomic Apps Script action or extend SECONDARY_QUARANTINE and _verify_required_accounting_journal to all financial operational actions; add missing-journal replay check on receive_raw_material and persist accounting_journal_ref to WorkforcePayments.

technical_explanation: GET /api/v2/transactions/status/{nonce} checks only get_current_user and passes actor_is_owner=is_owner(current_user) without verifying that the authenticated user initiated the transaction (local_tx['actor_user_id']) or holds RBAC read permission for target_tab. Confidential redaction only covers CONFIDENTIAL_TABS_NO_CACHE and SECURITY_NO_CACHE_TABS.
reproducible_scenario: Authenticate as FIELD_SALESMAN or FACTORY_WORKER and call GET /api/v2/transactions/status/{other_users_nonce} for an Accounts/Owner supplier payment, journal voucher, or customer sale. Endpoint returns HTTP 200 with allocated_id, tab_name, transaction_id, correlation_id, and recorded_at.
actual_impact: Cross-user IDOR / unauthorized operational and financial metadata disclosure across non-confidential tables.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — existing status endpoint tests only verify confidential payroll redaction for PA, not cross-user authorization on non-confidential transactions.
recommended_action: Enforce actor_user_id == current_user['user_id'] OR is_owner(current_user) (and module view RBAC for target_tab) in get_v2_transaction_status / check_transaction_status before returning transaction details.

technical_explanation: must_change_password is read from AuthUsers and included in JWT claims and /api/auth/me response, but neither get_current_user nor any middleware/router checks must_change_password before authorizing API calls.
reproducible_scenario: Reset a user password (setting must_change_password='true' in AuthUsers), log in via POST /api/auth/login to receive a bearer token, then call any authorized ERP endpoint (e.g., GET /api/sales or POST /api/sales) without calling /api/auth/change-password. Request succeeds with HTTP 200.
actual_impact: Forced password rotation for temporary/reset credentials is UI-only and completely bypassed by direct API requests.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — no backend security test verifies that must_change_password=true blocks non-password-change endpoints.
recommended_action: Enforce must_change_password server-side (e.g., in get_current_user or dedicated dependency/middleware) returning HTTP 403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED for all routes except /api/auth/me, /api/auth/change-password, and /api/auth/logout.

technical_explanation: When Owner approves PA-submitted RESET_PASSWORD, DEACTIVATE_USER, or role-changing UPDATE_USER requests via /api/approvals/requests/{id}/decision, _build_approval_execution_payload never includes sessions_revoked_at and decide_approval_request never updates _USER_REVOKED_AT (unlike direct Owner paths in user_service.py:998,1019,1067,1088,1141,1150).
reproducible_scenario: 1. User logs in and obtains valid JWT. 2. PA submits RESET_PASSWORD or UPDATE_USER (role downgrade) approval request. 3. Owner approves via POST /api/approvals/requests/{id}/decision. 4. User continues calling APIs with old JWT; token is not invalidated by sessions_revoked_at.
actual_impact: Stale/compromised sessions survive approval-workflow password resets and role changes until natural JWT expiry (8 hours).
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — approval workflow tests do not test post-approval invalidation of prior target-user JWTs.
recommended_action: Include sessions_revoked_at=now_iso_str in _build_approval_execution_payload for RESET_PASSWORD, DEACTIVATE_USER, and role-changing UPDATE_USER, and update _USER_REVOKED_AT[target_uid.lower()] after confirmed execution.

technical_explanation: None of fastapi, pydantic, jwt, gspread, or google.oauth2 are installed in the Python 3.11.2 environment. All 671 passing backend tests execute against pure-stdlib shims where MockBaseModel skips all Pydantic constraints/types, FastAPI route decorators become no-ops (bypassing Depends()), V2RouterProxy auto-injects idempotency headers, LocalAppsScriptSimulator auto-approves all 12 schema conflicts and simulates Apps Script atomicity in memory, and the real Uvicorn ASGI test is skipped.
reproducible_scenario: Run python3 -c 'import fastapi, pydantic, jwt, gspread' (all ImportError) and unittest discover (671 pass, 1 skip).
actual_impact: False test confidence: Pydantic validation bugs, FastAPI Depends() wiring bugs, real PyJWT edge cases, and real Apps Script Code.gs payload mismatches are completely invisible to this test run.
current_test_detection_status: SELF-MASKING — test suite reports 671/672 OK while exercising zero real framework/transport dependencies.
recommended_action: Run CI and pre-release verification in a real virtual environment with backend/requirements.txt installed (including TestClient HTTP tests verifying FastAPI Depends and Pydantic validation) plus staging verification against deployed Apps Script Code.gs (DB-008).

technical_explanation: Incomplete P1.8-007 remediation: all three endpoints define a domain 'status' field ('COMPLETED', 'APPROVED', 'OPEN') in their record dict, then spread **res LAST in the return dict ({**record, ..., **res}), causing bridge status='CONFIRMED' to overwrite the domain status.
reproducible_scenario: Invoke POST /api/quality/checks, POST /api/quality/customer-returns, or POST /api/quality/complaints. Returned JSON contains status='CONFIRMED' instead of 'COMPLETED', 'APPROVED', or 'OPEN'.
actual_impact: API contract corruption breaking frontend status badges/filters and violating Phase 1.8 repair P1.8-007.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — P1.8-007 tests only check stock.py and close_complaint_or_recall.
recommended_action: Place **res BEFORE domain record/status fields and expose bridge_status=res.get('status') on all three quality.py endpoints, matching stock.py:290 and quality.py:564.

technical_explanation: P1.8-005 appended a fresh random uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] to every reserve/release CAS nonce. While this avoids collision on a deliberate release-then-re-reserve sequence, an HTTP retry after a timeout/UNKNOWN on the SAME reserve or release attempt generates a brand new nonce instead of replaying the original nonce.
reproducible_scenario: Trigger HTTP 504 / UNKNOWN on reserve_credit_approval(req_id, sale_id) after Apps Script actually committed the reservation, then retry the same call. Retry sends a new nonce RESERVE-{req_id}-{sale_id}-{new_uuid} and fails with CAS_CONFLICT instead of idempotent replay.
actual_impact: Breaks deterministic idempotency for credit-approval reservation/release retries after UNKNOWN outcomes.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — existing tests verify release-then-re-reserve uniqueness but not timeout-retry replay on reserve/release.
recommended_action: Derive CAS nonces deterministically from a caller-supplied attempt/request nonce (or monotonic reservation version counter persisted on ApprovalRequests) rather than random uuid4 per call.

technical_explanation: verifyPayloadAgainstActiveLock only checks verifiedRetryAuthorizedNonces when params.requireVerifiedRetry is true (unknownOutcomeLock.ts:2489). Both apiFetch and apiRequest forward options.requireVerifiedRetry (default undefined), and zero production callers in src/ pass requireVerifiedRetry: true.
reproducible_scenario: Trigger an UNKNOWN outcome on any mutation via apiRequest/apiFetch, then immediately call apiRequest/apiFetch again with the same nonce and identical payload WITHOUT calling GET /api/v2/transactions/status/{nonce}. Transport layer permits the unverified retry to hit the network.
actual_impact: Relies solely on UI button disabling to prevent premature same-nonce retries before status verification; any programmatic retry or view lacking button lock bypasses status-first enforcement.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — frontend tests only test requireVerifiedRetry by explicitly passing requireVerifiedRetry: true in test harnesses.
recommended_action: Default requireVerifiedRetry to true inside apiFetch/apiRequest whenever an active UNKNOWN lock exists for the scope/nonce (allowing explicit opt-out only if strictly justified).

technical_explanation: All 5 mutating Employee Portal views submit writes via apiFetch('/api/workforce/...') but do NOT use useUnknownOutcomeGuard or render UnknownOutcomeBanner. When a write times out (504/disconnect), apiFetch locks scope 'workforce_view' in sessionStorage + memory; furthermore MyProjectsView and MyTasksView unconditionally clear setSubmitNonce('') when modals open/close.
reproducible_scenario: In MyAttendanceView or MyTasksView, simulate a 504 timeout on check-in or task submission. apiFetch locks 'workforce_view'. Employee sees only a plain text error with no 'Check Transaction Status' button. Closing/reopening modal resets nonce; next submit fails with HTTP 409 UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_LOCK_ACTIVE.
actual_impact: Employee is trapped in an unrecoverable frontend lock on workforce_view until closing the browser tab, unable to verify status or retry safely.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — test_mission51b1rf_persistence_and_fingerprint.ts test #18 only scans primary admin views in src/views/, skipping src/employee/views/.
recommended_action: Integrate useUnknownOutcomeGuard('workforce_view') (or dedicated employee-portal sub-scopes) and UnknownOutcomeBanner into all 5 mutating Employee Portal views, and guard setSubmitNonce('') with shouldBlockDraftNonceReset(unknownOutcome).

technical_explanation: (1) logout calls revoke_token(..., raise_on_failure=False) and returns HTTP 200 {ok: True, persisted: False} if the persistent RevokedTokens write fails, leaving tokens revocable only in process memory; (2) login brute-force protection _LOGIN_ATTEMPTS is a process-local dict keyed solely by username with no IP rate limit, no persistence across restarts, and no eviction of stale keys.
reproducible_scenario: (1) Cause RevokedTokens bridge write to fail during POST /api/auth/logout; endpoint still returns HTTP 200 ok=True, and after process restart the logged-out JWT is accepted again. (2) Spray failed logins with random usernames or across restarts to bypass lockout or grow _LOGIN_ATTEMPTS memory.
actual_impact: Weakened logout revocation durability and bypassable/memory-unbounded login brute-force throttling.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — logout tests do not assert non-2xx or fail-closed persistence semantics; no login memory-growth or IP-throttling tests exist.
recommended_action: Return HTTP 503 (or explicit non-ok failure) when persistent logout revocation fails in production, and add IP-based rate limiting with bounded LRU/TTL eviction for _LOGIN_ATTEMPTS.

technical_explanation: (1) ENDPOINT_SCOPE_RULES omits /api/v2/packaging and /api/v2/transactions, causing mutations without explicit lockScope to fail closed with AMBIGUOUS_TRANSACTION_SCOPE. (2) quality.py:456 hardcodes 5% GST (total_refund * Decimal('0.05')) on customer return journals without enforcing assert_ca_policy_approved('hsn_gst_tax_rates'). (3) closing.py:210 reads cached DailyClosing (fresh=False) on a write path and closing.py:105,141-142 uses float arithmetic for cash totals.
reproducible_scenario: (1) Call apiRequest('/api/v2/packaging/batches', {method:'POST', ...}) without explicit lockScope -> throws AMBIGUOUS_TRANSACTION_SCOPE. (2) Create a customer return while hsn_gst_tax_rates is PENDING_CA_APPROVAL -> posts 5% tax journal anyway. (3) Review a newly submitted closing while cache is warm -> 404 or stale status.
actual_impact: Blocked v2 packaging/reconcile mutations when lockScope is omitted; unapproved GST postings violating CA policy governance; stale-cache/float precision risk in daily cash closing.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — frontend tests do not exercise /api/v2/packaging or /api/v2/transactions without explicit lockScope; quality/closing tests do not assert CA GST gate or fresh=True on review.
recommended_action: Add /api/v2/packaging ('production_view') and /api/v2/transactions ('erp_operations_hub_view') to ENDPOINT_SCOPE_RULES; gate customer return GST posting on CA policy approval; use fresh=True and Decimal arithmetic in closing.py.

technical_explanation: workforce_migration.py blocks offline direct-write migration only when SALES_ENV=='production' (while config.py:17 defaults SALES_ENV to 'development'). Additionally, backend/scripts/run_staging_walkthrough.py:20 unconditionally mutates os.environ['SALES_TESTING']='1' at import time.
reproducible_scenario: Import run_staging_walkthrough in a process or run workforce_migration with SALES_ENV unset and SALES_ALLOW_OFFLINE_SHEETS_MIGRATION=1 against a caller-supplied writable spreadsheet object.
actual_impact: Defense-in-depth weakness if SALES_ENV is misconfigured/omitted on staging/production or if run_staging_walkthrough is accidentally imported.
current_test_detection_status: NOT DETECTED — migration tests run with SALES_TESTING=1 and default development env.
recommended_action: Default SALES_ENV fail-closed (or require explicit SALES_ENV=='local_dev' allowlist for offline migrations) and move SALES_TESTING mutation inside main() guarded by explicit CLI flag in run_staging_walkthrough.py.
